chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the NYC Council Committee on Technology hearing, asks everyone to silence electronic devices, states no one should approach the dais, and tells the chair they are ready to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens Committee on Technology hearing and requests silence

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council hearing for the Committee on Technology.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I would like to remind everyone to silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Also at this point, going forward, no one is supposed to approach the days.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we're ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin thanks Chair De La Rosa, calls the hearing a sequel to the initial AI hearing and last week's Committee of the Whole with major AI companies, and says NYC was first legislative body to hear from leading AI companies.
chapters.title: Speaker Julie Menin welcomes attendees and frames AI hearing as sequel

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm New York City Council Speaker Julie Menon.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I want to welcome everyone to today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I want to thank my colleague, the Technology Chair, Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We look forward to having a very fulsome hearing, and this is a sequel to our initial hearing on AI.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, the New York City Council continues a crucial conversation that continues from last week's Committee of the Whole with the world's largest AI companies.

chapters.summary: Menin says experts and public remain apprehensive about AI safety risks and companies, that answers last week reinforced need for safeguards, and that self-regulation is not supported.
chapters.title: Menin cites safety risks and rejects AI self-regulation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We were the first legislative body in the country that heard from the leading companies on their models that have captured as much attention as they have concern across the globe.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As we heard from both experts and the public, there is good reason to remain apprehensive about some of the safety risks around artificial intelligence as well as the companies behind these AI models.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The answers, quite frankly, that we received from last week's hearing only reinforce the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: for responsible safeguards to prevent harm.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And the idea that the companies would self-regulate is not a concept that we support at all.

chapters.summary: Menin says the Council wants to avoid stifling innovation, notes NYC's 400,000 tech jobs and AI capital status, and supports keeping jobs, research, startups, and economic growth in the city.
chapters.title: Menin balances innovation and NYC's growing AI economy

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: At the same time, we want to ensure that we are not stifling innovation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: New York City is rapidly growing as not only a tech capital, but also the AI capital of the world with over 400,000 jobs, more than the city of San Francisco, I might add.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we understand and we want to support keeping those jobs here in New York, supporting cutting-edge research, supporting startups, locating right here in our great city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we know that no matter how large or how small these various AI companies are, we know that those companies are vital to our city in terms of cutting edge research, medical breakthroughs, scientific discoveries,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and boosting economic growth.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But we cannot

chapters.summary: Menin says the city cannot wait for companies to act responsibly, cites models hacking companies and government websites, and welcomes SpaceX to testify under oath about evolving AI technology.
chapters.title: Menin warns of AI hacks and welcomes SpaceX under oath

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: wait for these companies to act responsibly when we see that some of these models are able to hack into other companies and also into government websites as well.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As we work to ensure that there are responsible, suitable safeguards in place following alarming public reports on AI,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We want to welcome SpaceX to this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It is not only New Yorkers who want to hear your testimony today, but people across the world.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we thank them for being here under oath to answer our questions about this evolving technology.

chapters.summary: Menin says AI leaders often warn about their own risks, then details proposed Council solutions including emergency preparedness, independent third-party validation free of conflicts, whistleblower incentives, and a plan for AI hacks into city systems.
chapters.title: Menin outlines Council AI safety bills

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Like I said at the hearing last week, these companies are developing technology that can reshape so many aspects of our lives.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And yet they are being led oftentimes by individuals who are publicly warning about the risks with their models.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we deserve to have those risks, those safety concerns answered, as well as a discussion about what are the best legislative solutions to address those risks.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This city council has proposed solutions to address, for example,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: emergency preparedness.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have bills to require third-party independent validation that is free from conflict of interest.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have a bill first in the nation to incentivize whistleblowers to come forward, as well as a bill to devise a plan for the scenario in which, in case AI hacks into city systems, as well as other bills as well.

chapters.summary: Menin says NYC can lead on AI safety while federal government fails to act, hopes local legislation spurs national standards, and compares AI oversight to FDA, FAA, and SEC regulation of other industries.
chapters.title: Menin calls for federal standards, compares AI to FDA/FAA/SEC

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I want to end by saying that at our hearing last week, we showed that New York City has demonstrated to the world that cities can and should take the lead on AI safety.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our federal government is simply failing to act.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Of course, we would like to see regulation at the federal level, and it is our fervent hope that by putting forward these legislative ideas, that it will ultimately

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: lead to the federal government coming up with national safety standards and regulations of AI.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Just as I said last week, we do not leave it to the pharmaceutical industry to self-regulate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have the FDA.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We do not leave it to the airline industry to self-regulate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have the FAA and an independent safety board.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: When there are safety concerns, we have the SEC that regulates the financial industry.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: With AI, what we are looking for is responsible safeguards to put in place.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: New York City has and always will be a leader in addressing the key issues that affect New Yorkers, and AI is simply no different.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I look forward to today's conversation.

chapters.summary: Menin thanks her team and staff for organizing the hearing and turns the floor over to Technology Committee Chair Carmen De La Rosa for her statement.
chapters.title: Menin thanks staff and turns to Chair De La Rosa

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I want to thank our team, our staff, for helping to organize this important hearing, and now I want to turn it over to Chair De La Rosa for a statement.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair De La Rosa welcomes attendees, notes last week's Committee of the Whole heard nearly 100 witnesses from OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Google, former employees, experts, and public, and says their message was that frontier AI poses risks.
chapters.title: Chair De La Rosa recaps prior AI hearing and witness concerns

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa, and I am the chair of the Committee on Technology.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Welcome to our hearing on continuing discussions about the risks posed by artificial intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Last week, in this very same room, in a meeting of the Committee of the Whole, we heard testimony from nearly 100 witnesses, including representatives from OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Google, their former employees,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: technical experts, academics, elected officials, and members of the public.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Despite their different points of view, their message was more

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: or less consistent.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: The pace and progress of frontier AI models does pose a risk.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Some called for frontier developers to slow down.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Others focused on alignment and control mechanisms, warnings of superintelligence, mass surveillance, and agentic policing, as well as political bias and discriminatory tendencies.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Several witnesses raised concerns about the loss of model control and others warned about the potential loss of jobs.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: However, much of the testimony returned to a common set of recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Transparency from AI developers, credible safety measures, third-party evaluators, and protection for personal data.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa says the Council wants AI's benefits in science, medicine, and productivity only with responsible development, and lists risks including bias, job displacement, censorship, deep fakes, and loss of control.
chapters.title: De La Rosa says benefits require responsible AI development

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Today, we plan to continue this conversation with another major AI company, SpaceX SI.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We want to reap the benefits of AI so long as these benefits come with responsible development and do not cost us our safety, our dignity, and our civil rights.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: AI has tremendous potential and can be a powerful tool for efficiency and innovation in science, medicine, and productivity.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: At the same time, it introduces important risks, including bias, discrimination, job displacement, censorship, digital forgeries, deep fakes, and concerns that may become

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: even more serious as AI agents become more capable.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa says AI tools must work as intended, people must understand training and failures, affected people need to contest machine decisions, and self-regulation by AI builders is insufficient; federal, state, and municipal intervention is necessary.
chapters.title: De La Rosa rejects self-regulation and calls for government intervention

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We should make sure

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: or AI tools work as intended, that we understand how they work, how they were trained, where they fail, and ensure that those affected have an opportunity to contest decisions made by machines.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: A framework where the very same people who build AI tools and have competing motives

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: are also expected to regulate themselves is wholly insufficient.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Intervention is necessary from federal, state, and municipal governments to protect our rights.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa thanks Technology Committee staff, Legislative Council Irene Bayofsky, Policy Analyst Eric Brown, her office team, and Speaker Menin's team, and recognizes Council Member Maloney.
chapters.title: De La Rosa thanks staff and recognizes Council Member Maloney

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Once again, I look forward to hearing more from industry experts about what solutions are possible to ensure New Yorkers can fully benefit

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: from technological advancement without compromising civil rights, safety, and privacy.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I now like to thank the Technology Committee staff, Legislative Council Irene Bayofsky, and Policy Analyst Eric Brown, as well as my Chief of Staff James Burke, Legislative Director Hiba Imad,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Comms Director Frey Familia, and Speaker Menon's entire team for their continued work on this important matter.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I'd also like to recognize some of the council members that have joined us.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Council member Maloney.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And that's it for now.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: More to come.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I now turn it back to Speaker Menon and the committee council.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin turns the hearing over to Council staff, who asks Gabriela Castillo-Madrid to affirm that she will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth; she answers yes.
chapters.title: Council staff administers affirmation to Gabriela Castillo-Madrid

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair De La Rosa.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm now going to pass it over to council to do the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Castillo-Madrid, you may answer yes after the question.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth in your testimony before this committee?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin your testimony.

chapters.summary: Castillo-Madrid, on SpaceX's Government Affairs team, introduces herself, describes SpaceX's reusable rockets, Starlink, and missions, and says SpaceX acquired XAI to blend infrastructure expertise with frontier AI and superintelligence development.
chapters.title: Gabriela Castillo-Madrid introduces SpaceX and XAI acquisition

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Madam Speaker, Chair de la Rosa, and members of the Committee on Technology, thank you for the opportunity to participate today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: My name is Gabriela Castillo-Madrid, and I am part of the Government Affairs team at SpaceX.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: My team's responsibility is to maintain a close relationship between the teams building our advanced technologies, including Frontier SI models, and the communities that use and benefit from them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: SpaceX has grown from a startup nearly 25 years ago to a company that launches more rockets and orbits more satellites every year than any other nation or company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Developing rapidly reusable rockets has enabled SpaceX to dramatically lower the cost of launch and make new NASA missions and science possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Including regular and reliable crew and cargo missions to the International Space Station and the upcoming Artemis mission to the Moon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our Starlink satellites now make possible reliable broadband connectivity across over 160 countries, including to locations where high-speed internet has never been available before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: SpaceX's mission is to make humanity multi-planetary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Earlier this year, SpaceX acquired XAI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Blending SpaceX's deep technical expertise building large complex infrastructure and complex space systems with the development of superintelligence and frontier SI models.

chapters.summary: Castillo-Madrid says safety is core to Grok from pre-training through deployment, describes control, prevention, mitigation, analysis, and correction, says models are trained to refuse dangerous activity, evaluated for misuse, monitored after deployment, and not released if insufficiently robust.
chapters.title: Castillo-Madrid describes Grok safety approach and controls

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Just as we have done with Space Launch and Human Spaceflight, SpaceX SI puts safety first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: As a mother, I know the risks New Yorkers worry about are often those close to home, protecting our children, preventing harmful content, and stopping misuse of everyday SI tools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And I can assure you that safety is core to how we build Grok, from pre-training through deployment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our approach starts with a simple idea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: A super intelligent system built to seek the truth and understand the universe as it actually is will be more safe, reliable, and useful to the people who rely on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our safety work is how we make sure that holds up in practice by focusing on control, prevention, mitigation, analysis, and correction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Concretely, that effort begins well before a model is released for public use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We train our models to refuse assistance with dangerous activity, evaluate it for risks including misuse of our terms of service, attempts to get around

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: safeguards, and loss of control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We monitor systems after deployment and we do not release models we believe are insufficiently robust against misuse by bad actors or follow meaningful human control.

chapters.summary: Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX publishes a Frontier AI Framework and model cards, performs annual risk assessments, investigates and reports problems when required, and argues AI can improve research, public information, and city services if safe and accountable.
chapters.title: Castillo-Madrid cites transparency, annual risk assessments, and benefits

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: These practices are outlined in our publicly available Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework along with each new model card.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Which describes how we assessed and reduced these risks across the model's lifecycle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We also perform a full risk assessment of our practices and controls at least once per year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We believe transparency is fundamental to creating a safer ecosystem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: When something goes wrong, we investigate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Work to fix it, and report it to the authorities when required.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Use well, SI can help improve the lives of the people of New York by speeding up research, making public information easier to find and use, and helping city agencies and residents with complex tasks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Those benefits only matter if the systems remain safe and accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: This is why we continue to invest in evaluation, monitoring, and human control, and why we want to work with policymakers on practical, evidence-based protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I look forward to answering your questions today and continuing the conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin asks about Dario Amodei's article warning that AI agents could take over the internet with a botnet causing billions in damage, and Elon Musk's reply that Dario is right; Castillo-Madrid says she is unfamiliar and repeats SpaceX's safety and human-control commitments.
chapters.title: Menin questions Castillo-Madrid on Dario Amodei's AI botnet warning

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we have a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On September 12th, Daria Mode authored an article entitled, We Must Pace the Frontiers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: here stating that within six to 12 months, a swarm of AI agents, quote, could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage, end quote.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Was he correct here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I wouldn't, I'm not familiar with that statement in particular.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: What I will say is safety is core to SpaceX SI, and that goes from pre-training through release.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: So people stay in control of our systems at every stage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We do not release models we do not believe are safe and that we cannot keep under meaningful human control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And if a model does not meet that bar, we hold it back and strengthen the model and safeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We train models to ensure they don't assist with dangerous activity and evaluate them for misuse.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So then why did Elon Musk state on X in a post in response to those comments, Dario is right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I believe we're optimistic about SI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We obviously take the risk seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Elon has been one of the earliest and most prominent voices in warning about SI risk and calling for oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: But we are extremely positive about what can be achieved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We believe that superintelligence can help people solve problems that were previously beyond reach, accelerating scientific discovery and expanding knowledge and creating new opportunities for human progress.

chapters.summary: Menin asks whether SpaceX will agree not to release any model that failed internal or third-party validated tests; Castillo-Madrid says the public can have confidence in pre-release testing and safeguard stacks, and that gaps are tightened before release.
chapters.title: Menin presses on whether unsafe models would be withheld after failed tests

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So you've just mentioned that the company will not release any models that are not, quote unquote, safe.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So will you agree then that the company will not release any model that failed an internal or third party validated test?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Yeah, the public can take great confidence in the testing that occurs before models are released and the safeguard stacks that are surround model deployments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: As models get more capable, we often find gaps that need stronger protections and we also tighten those before the model goes out.

chapters.summary: Menin cites an Axios report that major AI companies privately gamed out a public and political revolt after a catastrophic AI event, and asks whether SpaceX has assessed worst-case financial, cybersecurity, or physical harm; Castillo-Madrid says she is not familiar with specifics but takes catastrophic risk seriously.
chapters.title: Menin asks about Axios report on catastrophic AI scenario planning

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So to that end, Axios reported on October 9th, the major AI companies were, quote, privately gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt after a catastrophic AI event, end quote.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Has your company ever conducted an internal assessment or worst case outcome causing substantial financial cybersecurity or physical harm?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any specific.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: But I will say that we take catastrophic risk very seriously.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I just want to interrupt you when you say you're not familiar with any specifics.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, the question is, has Axios had this reporting saying that many of the frontier companies were gaming these tests out?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Is that something that SpaceX AI has done?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Or not?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I cannot speak to a specific test.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: What I can say is that we do obviously test our systems and make sure there's continuous evaluation and human oversight rather than accepting any unacceptable risk.

chapters.summary: Menin asks whether SpaceX is aware of any safety or cybersecurity incident not yet publicly reported; Castillo-Madrid says she is not aware of unreported incidents and again says SpaceX would not release a model without thorough review and meaningful human control.
chapters.title: Menin asks about unreported safety or cybersecurity incidents

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Is the company aware of any safety or cybersecurity incident?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Or any evidence of such an incident that has not yet been publicly reported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any incidents that have not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, I just find this answer not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, you're not aware.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Is the company, I'm going to rephrase the question, is the company aware?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Safety is the core of everything we do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And like I mentioned, we wouldn't release a model that hasn't gone through thorough review and making sure that we can keep it under meaningful human control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And like I said, if the model does not meet that bar, we hold it back and strengthen the model and the safeguards around it.

chapters.summary: Menin cites Grok Imagine's spicy mode and integration of image editing that generated millions of sexualized images, including about 23,000 appearing to depict young children; Castillo-Madrid calls the conduct unacceptable and cites strict controls, CSAM prohibitions, and NCMEC reporting.
chapters.title: Menin challenges SpaceX over Grok sexualized images of women and children

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So when you say that you have the company doesn't release any model that is not safe, in August 2025, the company launched.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Grok imagined with a quote unquote spicy mode for explicit content.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: In late December 2025, the company integrated Grok's image editing features into the platform, allowing users to alter photos of real people.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Within days, Grok generated millions of sexualized images of women and children.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Approximately 23,000 images appeared to depict young children.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So how do you then, when you say you're not releasing a model that is safe, do you think that that is acceptable conduct?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: To be clear, that's not acceptable conduct, and we're all on the same side of this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: GROC has strict controls in place to prevent the sexualization of children or real people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We've always had prohibited CSAM and NCI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: When bad actors go around our safeties, we make sure that we catch them and report them to authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We actually have...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: A great partnership with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And just this year, we have made over 100,000 reports that have resulted in almost 300 arrests.

chapters.summary: Menin asks whether a user can get Grok to show a real person nude or sexualized; Castillo-Madrid repeats that Grok has strict controls; Menin says she and her team entered her name and got a sexualized image, calls the answer unacceptable, and Castillo-Madrid says no one should have such images made without consent.
chapters.title: Menin says her own name produced a sexualized Grok image

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So today, can a user get Grok, the Grok app, or Grok Imagine to show a real person nude in their underwear or in a sexualized pose?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Grog has strict controls in place to prevent the sexualization of children or real people.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm going to completely push back on it.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, just this more.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: myself and my team, we put our own name, my own name into Grok, and there's absolutely like a sexualized image of myself.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So if it can happen to me, it can happen to any woman.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I completely discount what you're saying that Grok has solved this problem.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, it's completely unacceptable when these kind of sexualized images are readily available.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: To be clear, no one should have sexualized images made of them without their consent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And our policies prohibit that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Any specific cases I can't speak of, but I will say, like I said before, we have a very bright line and a grok cannot be used to exploit minors, commit crimes, or generate illegal content.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So then how is it that within a second I could find a sexualized image of myself on using Grok?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Madam Speaker, I can't speak to that specific instance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: What I can say is that we do have strict controls, and I'm happy to get our safety team to look into that specific instance.

chapters.summary: Menin asks how many complaints or takedown requests SpaceX has received about Grok-generated sexualized images; Castillo-Madrid says over 100,000 reports went to NCMEC and that SpaceX sued three users facing criminal charges, while Menin says the ease of finding the image shows the technology allows it.
chapters.title: Menin questions NCMEC reports and takedown requests

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And if you had to report, you mentioned 100,000 instances.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Doesn't that mean then by that very definition that the technology allows it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our reports are meant to catch bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Unfortunately, there's always going to be bad actors and folks trying to get around safeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And our work is to catch them and get them to the right authorities.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: How many reports, complaints, takedown requests, or demands from depicted individuals has the company received concerning grok-generated sexualized images?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: You mentioned the 100,000.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Does that encompass all of the complaints that people have filed on this issue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: That over 100,000 reports are specifically sent to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: In the case that you're explaining, the reports were caught and actions were taken.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We even took three federal lawsuits against the users that were already facing criminal charges for their abuse of Grok in creating illegal content.

chapters.summary: Menin asks what safeguards Grok will implement moving forward after she found a sexualized image of herself within seconds; Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX will strengthen systems and has strict controls, but cannot speak to the specific case.
chapters.title: Menin asks what safeguards Grok will add for sexualized images

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But then the fact that within seconds I could find this image of myself, what type of safeguards is Grok going to do then moving forward?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Well, like I said, we'll make sure that we're strengthening our systems, and I cannot speak to that particular case, but we do have strict controls in place to prevent the sexualization of children or real people.

chapters.summary: Menin cites July 2025 Grok chatbot posts including one calling itself 'MechaHitler' and asks what steps SpaceX AI has taken to prevent such instances; Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX trains models against dangerous activity, evaluates misuse, and monitors after deployment in an iterative process.
chapters.title: Menin asks about Grok's anti-Semitic posts

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: In July 2025, Grok's chatbot published a series of anti-Semitic posts, including one in which it called itself Mecca Hitler.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: What steps has SpaceX AI taken to prevent these instances from happening?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We take steps to strengthen all of our safeties, and we train models to ensure they don't assist with dangerous activity, evaluate them for misuse, which was the case, and attempts to get around safeguards and loss of control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And we monitor after deployment as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We understand that it has to be an iterative process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: As models evolve, our safety has evolved with it as well.

chapters.summary: Menin repeatedly asks how many SpaceX AI employees are dedicated to safety, security, and cybersecurity risks; Castillo-Madrid says she does not have the number and that safety is embedded company-wide, and Menin demands the answer by the end of testimony.
chapters.title: Menin asks how many employees work on AI safety

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: How many SpaceX AI employees are principally dedicated to identifying, evaluating, and mitigating safety, security, and cybersecurity risks associated with your frontier AI models?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We have a robust safety team, and safety is...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm sorry, how many?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We have a robust safety team and safety is embedded into our...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But how many?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: How many employees?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I don't have the number with me right now, but what I can say is that safety is at the core of everything we do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And it's core to not just our engineers and our safety, but everybody in the company is bought into the importance of safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Like I mentioned earlier, we're launching rockets into space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And obviously to get to that place, we need to make sure that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Safety is at the forefront of everything we do.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This seems like a very rudimentary question, how many people are dedicated to

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: on the safety team relative to the company as a whole?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This seems like a very basic question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: The way we see it is everybody is in charge of safety, and we make sure that if anybody sees something, they say it and report it quick.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I think it would assure the public far more if we got a straightforward answer on actually how many people at the company are dedicated to evaluating the safety models.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a very basic question, and I'm going to ask that by the end of the testimony, you provide that answer to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Madam Speaker, we'll get on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Menin asks whether SpaceX AI uses financially independent evaluators with no ties to the company before deploying dangerous models; Castillo-Madrid cites White House accord commitments to internal controls and independent external evaluators but does not name any auditors.
chapters.title: Menin asks about independent evaluators free of conflicts

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Does SpaceX AI use financially independent evaluators that do not have any direct or indirect financial ties to the company before testing or deploying a potentially dangerous AI model?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: As part of the White House accord, we agreed on certain agreements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Company responsibility is one of them, internal controls, internal oversight team, and independent external evaluators is one of them as well, as well as board level oversight.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I guess yes or no, are there independent third-party validators who are validating, who are free from any conflict of interest?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: who are validating the new models.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We're working on partnerships with independent external auditors or evaluators to assess model capabilities, controls, and safeguards.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And are you going to be disclosing who those auditors are?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: That's not up to me, but I'll make sure that I'll get an answer for you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Again, I think, you know, the idea that there is self-regulation is not something that is making people feel comfortable at all.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so as a most rudimentary measure to have independent third party.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Validators who are free from conflict of interest, which is actually what one of our bills exactly does, is something that we believe you should be able to answer.

chapters.summary: Menin cites rogue Anthropic agents filing a false police report and visa applications, and asks who bears legal responsibility if swarms of agents cause harm; Castillo-Madrid says AI is not self-regulated, existing laws apply, and SpaceX would not use AI as a legal defense.
chapters.title: Menin asks who bears legal responsibility for rogue AI agents

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last week, rogue anthropic AI agents filed a false police report in Philadelphia.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another agent attempted to file 20 false visa applications.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thankfully, the incidents did not go beyond that, but they raised the prospect of swarms of rogue agents filing thousands of false reports with government and businesses alike.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If that harm occurs, who bears the legal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Madam Speaker, to be clear, we're not self-regulated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: SI is not a self-regulated industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We operate within a framework of existing laws, and we would never use SI as an excuse for something or as a legal defense.

chapters.summary: Menin says there is no federal AI regulation, no independent federal agency validating safety models, and no law on the books; Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX is open to working with policymakers and abides by regulatory requirements, and that what is illegal without superintelligence is illegal with it.
chapters.title: Menin says no federal AI regulation exists

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But don't you agree there's no national, there's no federal regulation of AI right now?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: There's no law on the books that is regulating it.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: There's no agency that is independent, federal agency that is in charge of validating the safety models.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: None of that exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: That is why we're open to working with policymakers to make sure that we find common sense, technically feasible solutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: But we do abide by regulatory requirements and government oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And what's illegal without superintelligence is also illegal with it.

chapters.summary: Menin returns to the rogue agent example and asks who bears legal responsibility and whether SpaceX AI has catastrophic insurance; Castillo-Madrid says she is not familiar with the specific case or insurance policies, and Menin says this is a simple yes-or-no question.
chapters.title: Menin asks about liability and catastrophic insurance

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But going back to the question I asked earlier of the example of the rogue anthropic agents filing the false reports, who bears legal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that specific case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We're responsible if you're following the law when it comes to SpaceXSI and existing laws apply to AI just as it applies to anything else.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So if SpaceX AI causes either material injury, physical damage, you know, God forbid, a death, something cataclysmic,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: then the company bears responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We're responsible for following the law.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Does SpaceX AI have catastrophic insurance in the event of one of these catastrophes happening?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the specifics of our insurance policies and what we have and we don't.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Again, this is a very basic question.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's what I asked the other companies last week.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a simple yes or no.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Either the company has insurance liability in the event of a catastrophic risk.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Around their AI or not?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I just don't want to misspeak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I do understand the question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I just, I don't have the specifics on our insurance policies.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Menin pauses her questioning and passes the floor to Chair De La Rosa for her questions and to other members.
chapters.title: Menin turns questioning to Chair De La Rosa

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm going to pause for a minute and pass it to the chair for her questions and to other members at this point.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa confirms Castillo-Madrid is an attorney and Senior Manager of Global Government Affairs, asks whether she has access to safety numbers and data, and Castillo-Madrid says she would have to get back to her team.
chapters.title: De La Rosa asks Castillo-Madrid about her role and access to data

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Ms.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Castillo-Madrid, you're the Senior Manager of Global Government Affairs.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Are you an attorney?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And in your role, these questions that the speaker just asked in terms of, you know, the numbers,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Do you have access to that type of information?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: To be clear, although I am a barred attorney, I don't practice law at SpaceX or I haven't practiced law in reality for a long time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Almost a decade.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Okay, but do you have access to this type of information, like some of the numbers the speaker has asked for?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I'm imagining, as someone who's a senior manager of global affairs, you deal with regulators, you deal with elected officials on a worldwide basis.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: These are very simple questions that this council is asking.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So my question to you is, do you have access to either yourself having direct data that you could give this council, or the people who are in charge of having such information?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I would have to get back to the team and make sure that we have what you need or what you're seeking.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Hopefully Congress also calls you up to testify, and when they do, I hope you have those answers.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa asks what risk assessments SpaceX performs, what it has reported to authorities, and when reporting is required; Castillo-Madrid describes ongoing testing from pre-training to deployment and says she lacks specifics on reports but will get back to the team.
chapters.title: De La Rosa questions risk assessments and reports to authorities

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You testified that risk assessments happen once a year.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And you said, and we report to the authorities when required.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: What type of risk assessments happen?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And what have you reported to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And when is it required?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Like I said, we don't release any models that we don't believe are safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: So the risk assessment, that's like an ongoing risk assessment, but we do test our models well before release, and it's just a continuing process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Safety protocols have to stay at a scale with the capability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: of the technology and the public can take great confidence that we're testing that our testing occurs at every stage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: So from pre-training to deployment and beyond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We also keep watching systems after deployment and only release models we believe we can keep under meaningful human control.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: What have you reported to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: What instances have been?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I don't have the specifics on reports to authorities, but I will say that whenever it's required, we're ready to do so.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: When is it required?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: By law.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Have you reported any incidents to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any incidents that we have had within the timeframe that we're discussing right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: But like I said, I can get back to the team and get you an answer.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So what you testified is a protocol or a procedure that is in place in case it's necessary, but it hasn't been necessary to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: To my knowledge, we haven't had any rogue agents or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Obviously, the speaker did mention something that happened earlier this year, and we made reports around it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And I even mentioned how we work with law enforcement, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We do have a great partnership with them that has been going on for a long time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: time and we take very seriously our partnerships with law enforcement to make sure that any bad actors are caught and are kept off of the different platforms.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa asks whether Castillo-Madrid would be notified if an incident were reported to authorities; Castillo-Madrid says the legal team would be better positioned and that she will report back, and De La Rosa asks why the legal team is not there.
chapters.title: De La Rosa asks why SpaceX legal team is not present

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And in your role, if something were to be reported to the authorities, would you be notified?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I don't want to speak out of line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I think the legal team would be a better.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So why is the legal team not here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm here to answer your questions as best as I can, and I'm happy to report anything, anything that you need more of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: After the hearing.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa asks how many whistleblowers SpaceX has fired; Castillo-Madrid says she is not aware of any cases and cites industry-standard protections and no retaliation against whistleblowers.
chapters.title: De La Rosa asks how many whistleblowers SpaceX has fired

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: How many whistleblowers has your company fired?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any cases of whistleblowers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We have industry standard protections for the safety and no retaliation against whistleblowers.

chapters.summary: Menin interjects that former SpaceX employee Devin Kim was reportedly fired after raising serious safety concerns and asks why; Castillo-Madrid says she is not aware of that specific case, and Menin says she finds that not credible under oath.
chapters.title: Menin challenges Castillo-Madrid on Devin Kim's firing

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I just want to interject for a minute because Devin Kim

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: One of your former employees was reportedly fired after he sounded the alarm about serious safety concerns.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware with that specific case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: What I will say is safety is at the core of everything we do, and we take safety very seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And everybody has an ability to say something when they see something.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We have even for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: before a lunch, everybody receives an email from leadership saying, if you have any reason to believe there's a safety concern, please let us know and we'll delay anything that's happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: So like I said, we take safety very seriously and we'll delay any release of a model.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But if you take safety very seriously, why would Devin Kim, who sounded the alarm about major safety issues, which he brought to leadership as soon as he did so, he was fired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that specific case.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I don't understand if you can say you're not, I mean, you're under oath.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So you, under oath, you're not aware of anything regarding Devin Kim.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that specific case, Madam Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, okay, it was widely, it's been in the news, it's been on social media.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I just find that not credible.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'll pass it back over to the chair.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa says Castillo-Madrid's lack of knowledge about the firing erodes public trust and notes the Council had to use subpoena power; she then asks whether SpaceX sells or deploys AI for hiring, tenant screening, lending, schools, or city agencies, and Castillo-Madrid says models are widely available.
chapters.title: De La Rosa criticizes evasiveness and asks about NYC AI deployments

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, you just finished saying that the company sends company-wide emails.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Before lunch and something of this nature that has been reported that this council already has the information but yet you're an internal

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: agent of your company and you have no idea about this firing it's hard to believe and at the crux of this issue is trust and the public's trust

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: and when you all come before us and do not answer our questions or purport to not know

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: It erodes the public's trust, and that is part of the problem and how we got here.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And it's also shameful that, you know, the speaker had to use,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: the council's subpoena power to even get you here.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We could have done this last week for the answers that you're giving us today.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Does your company, well, first of all, let me acknowledge that we've been joined by Councilmember Narcisse.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Does your company currently sell or deploy AI systems in New York City to employers for hiring, to landlords for screening prospective tenants, to lenders, to schools, to city agencies?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our models are widely available to the public.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Do you sell them to the city of New York?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of specific cases where we have sold or not sold.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not part of the team specifically, but I will say that all our models are widely available for the public.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Your global government affairs, the city of New York is a government entity.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I'm quite confused about your role in the company.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa asks whether SpaceX sells or deploys AI to law enforcement, the Department of Defense, or other agencies, and whether all cloud infrastructure is in the U.S.; Castillo-Madrid says it partners with multiple U.S. and local agencies, lacks an exhaustive list, and believes infrastructure is in the U.S.
chapters.title: De La Rosa asks about law enforcement, defense partnerships, and cloud location

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Does your company sell or deploy AI systems to law enforcement agencies?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: We have great partnerships with governments across the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And internationally.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Law enforcement agencies, the Department of Defense, any other agencies?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: That includes multiple agencies across U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Government and local ones.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Do you know which ones?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I don't have an exhaustive list of our partnerships with U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Government, but we're proud to partner with them.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Is all of your cloud infrastructure located in the United States?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If not, which other countries is your infrastructure located?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I believe all of our infrastructure is located in the United States.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa condemns the sexualized image of Speaker Menin, asks about UK Parliament member Jess Asado's lawsuit against SpaceX, and cites reports that SpaceX set aside $530 million for potential litigation over Grok sexualized imagery; Castillo-Madrid says she cannot discuss pending cases or predict litigation.
chapters.title: De La Rosa questions deepfakes, Jess Asado case, and litigation reserves

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Going back to the speaker's line of questionings around deep fakes and sexual images, and I'm sorry, Madam Speaker, that your image was used in that way, you know, is disgraceful.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And we heard last week the very moving testimony of Jess Asado, who is a member of the parliament in the UK, who is, my understanding, is suing your company.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Do you have any comments on Member Asado's case?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Yes, to be clear, I'm a woman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: No one should have sexualized images made of them without their consent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And our policies prohibit that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Obviously, her case is pending, so I can't discuss the specifics there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: But I do want to say we're all on the same side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Bad actors should not be allowed to do and go around the safeguards that we have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And that's why we continuously improve those safeguards and make sure that Grok.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: is not used to exploit minors, commit crimes, or generate illegal content.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: It was reported as of December that SpaceX has set aside $530 million

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: for potential litigation laws, some of which could stem from ongoing complaints filed against its AI unit over sexualized imagery generated by Grok chatbots.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: There are several lawsuits filed against you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Do you anticipate more cases filed, although there are restrictions in place?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I couldn't predict the litigation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: What I will say is that we are strengthening the systems to ensure that nobody is going around our safeguards and using grok for illegal activity.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: But you anticipated $530 million in losses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the specifics on that, but I will say is I can't predict what will or not happen in that litigation front.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa says being able to pull up a sexualized image of Speaker Menin that morning shows SpaceX's safety line is not real, especially when women's bodies are sexualized; Castillo-Madrid repeats that Grok has strict controls and she cannot speak to specific cases.
chapters.title: De La Rosa says sexualized images contradict safety claims

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You know, the speaker was just sharing her own experience, and it is disgusting.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And, you know, you're a woman and I appreciate you being here.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: But the fact that we could pull an image up like that this morning means that whatever safeguards in place and this line that you keep giving us about safety is a priority, that is not safety.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: When a woman's body is being utilized in the way that these pictures are sexualizing the leaders of our city,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: That's not safety.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So in that case,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: How is this line about safety being implemented when just this morning we were able to pull up this picture?

chapters.summary: Menin says she found a sexualized image of herself in under 30 seconds on regular Grok, not spicy mode, and that successive prompts made it more sexualized; Castillo-Madrid apologizes and says Grok's policies prohibit such use, but Menin calls it unacceptable.
chapters.title: Menin details finding sexualized image in 30 seconds on regular Grok

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yeah, and I just want to build on that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Like literally within 30 seconds, and that was not even on the spicy mode.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This was on regular grok.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We literally asked regular grok to pull up a sexualized image, and a sexualized image comes up.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That is available for all to see, for my daughter to see, for anyone to see.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I just don't understand how you can say that there are these safety monitors when clearly it was less than 30 seconds to just pull up this image.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: All I can say is Grok has strict controls in place to prevent the sexualization of children and real people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I do apologize that you had to go through that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: And like I said, I don't think anybody should be put in that position.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our policies prohibit it for that reason.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's not that I had to go through it.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I literally just asked Rock to pull up the image and it came up.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I mean, this is now, it's not just about for elected officials, it's for anyone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So it's just unacceptable.

chapters.summary: Menin says Castillo-Madrid's canned safety answers are belied by the firing of Devin Kim, president of the Center for AI Safety and an early SpaceX AI employee; Castillo-Madrid says she is not familiar with the details of his termination.
chapters.title: Menin returns to Devin Kim's firing and safety claims

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And the other thing that I just want to say is that when you say you keep giving us this canned answer about safety, safety, safety,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: getting back to Devin Kim, his title was president of the Center for AI Safety.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He was one of the early employees at SpaceX AI.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's just completely not believable that you are not.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: aware of the circumstances around his firing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I understand your frustration, Madam Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Unfortunately, like the chairwoman said, there's a lot that I cover, and I want to make sure that I'm being as truthful as I can, and I answer the question with the facts that I know.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But if he's the president of the AI safety, I don't understand how you could not be familiar with his termination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the details of why he's no longer in the company.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa notes SpaceX challenged Minnesota's restrictions on AI tools enabling nonconsensual sexual imagery and asks where legal responsibility lies; Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX is not fighting a ban on nonconsensual deepfakes but opposes the law's reach to lawful content.
chapters.title: De La Rosa asks about Minnesota law and liability for nonconsensual imagery

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Your company has challenged in court Minnesota's restrictions on AI tools that enable non-consensual sexual imagery.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Where do you believe legal responsibility should lie when a user employs your model to create such material?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Is it with the user, the developer, or both?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And what obligations should developers have to prevent the misuse?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: To be clear, we're not fighting a ban on non-consensual deepfakes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our own policies prohibit notifying real people's image without their consent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: Our concern with that specific law you cite is that the law extends to lawful content, and the Eighth Circuit agrees, and they temporarily blocked enforcement because of that.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa says Speaker Menin did not consent to her sexualized image and it was found in 15 seconds, asking what responsibility the company bears; Castillo-Madrid says SpaceX supports protections from harmful synthetic media while allowing legitimate creative and scientific uses.
chapters.title: De La Rosa presses company responsibility for nonconsensual imagery

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So in your opinion, it's not your job to restrict sexual imagery, just sexual imagery that's done without consent.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: But here we have, for example, the Speaker of the City Council who has not given her consent for the use of her image, and yet we find it in 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So what responsibility lies with your company in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriela Castillo Madrid
utterances.text: I mean, we support measures that protect the public from harmful synthetic media while allowing legitimate creative and scientific uses of our product.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: This is not a scientific use, FYI.
